morphology.shape: Diplococci — kidney-bean/coffee-bean shaped with flattened adjacent sides

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human genital, rectal, pharyngeal, and conjunctival mucosa
habitat.hostAssociation: Strict human pathogen with no other reservoir
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Fragile outside the host; does not survive well in the environment

microscopy.appearance: Gram-negative diplococci, often seen intracellularly within neutrophils in symptomatic urethritis

culture.media: Thayer-Martin (chocolate agar with antibiotics) or chocolate agar, incubated with 5-10% CO2
culture.hemolysis: Not applicable — grown on enriched, non-blood media

identificationClues: Intracellular diplococci within neutrophils on a symptomatic urethral/cervical smear
Grows on Thayer-Martin selective medium with added CO2
Ferments glucose but not maltose — distinguishes it from N. meningitidis

clinicalImportance.transmission: Sexual contact; vertical transmission to neonates during delivery
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the most common bacterial sexually transmitted infections worldwide; increasing antimicrobial resistance is a growing clinical concern
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Intracellular Gram-negative diplococci on a symptomatic male urethral smear is highly suggestive; culture or NAAT is used for confirmation

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Oxidase positive; ferments glucose but not maltose
examFacts.importantTest: Gram stain showing intracellular diplococci; culture on Thayer-Martin medium
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Ferments glucose only (not maltose), distinguishing it from N. meningitidis, which ferments both
